question_text:
A specimen of magnesium having a rectangular cross section of dimensions $3.2 \mathrm{~mm} \times 19.1 \mathrm{~mm}\left(\frac{1}{8} \mathrm{in} . \times \frac{3}{4}\right.$ in.) is deformed in tension. Using the load-elongation data shown in the following table. Compute the modulus of resilience.

| Load |  | Length |  |
| :--: | :--: | :--: | :--: |
| $l b{f}$ | N | in. | mm |
| 0 | 0 | 2.500 | 63.50 |
| 310 | 1380 | 2.501 | 63.53 |
| 625 | 2780 | 2.502 | 63.56 |
| 1265 | 5630 | 2.505 | 63.62 |
| 1670 | 7430 | 2.508 | 63.70 |
| 1830 | 8140 | 2.510 | 63.75 |
| 2220 | 9870 | 2.525 | 64.14 |
| 2890 | 12,850 | 2.575 | 65.41 |
| 3170 | 14,100 | 2.625 | 66.68 |
| 3225 | 14,340 | 2.675 | 67.95 |
| 3110 | 13,830 | 2.725 | 69.22 |
| 2810 | 12,500 | 2.775 | 70.49 |
|  |  |  |  |The unit of the answer is J/m^3.
response:
## Solution

The **modulus of resilience** is the strain energy per unit volume absorbed up to the elastic limit (proportional limit):

$$U_r = \int_0^{\varepsilon_y} \sigma\, d\varepsilon = \frac{\sigma_y^2}{2E} = \frac{1}{2}\sigma_y \varepsilon_y$$

**Step 1 — Cross-sectional area and gauge length**
$$A_0 = 3.2 \times 19.1 = 61.12\ \text{mm}^2, \quad L_0 = 63.50\ \text{mm}$$

**Step 2 — Identify the elastic (linear) region**

Computing engineering stress $\sigma = P/A_0$ and strain $\varepsilon = \Delta L/L_0$, the data are linear through the first four points (0–5630 N); the slope drops sharply afterward (49,350 → 23,376 MPa), so the **proportional limit** is at 5630 N:

$$\sigma_y = \frac{5630}{61.12} = 92.1\ \text{MPa}, \qquad \varepsilon_y = \frac{63.62-63.50}{63.50} = 0.00189$$

**Step 3 — Elastic modulus** (linear regression on the elastic points)
$$E \approx 48{,}790\ \text{MPa} \approx 48.8\ \text{GPa}$$

**Step 4 — Modulus of resilience**
$$U_r = \tfrac{1}{2}\sigma_y \varepsilon_y = \tfrac{1}{2}(92.1\times10^6)(0.00189) \approx 8.7\times10^4\ \text{J/m}^3$$

$$\boxed{8.7\times10^{4}}$$
